geometry.locator: The surface detector array of the Telescope Array experiment, site-description section
geometry.note: 'verified': representation is 'surveyed' from a rank<=10 (detector_paper) source.
geometry.quote: The TA site is located in the desert about 1400 m above sea level centered at 39.3 N and 112.9 W in Millard County, Utah, USA

method: Coordinate taken from the TA surface-detector array paper's own description of the site centre (39.3 N, 112.9 W, one-decimal-degree precision), fetched via the ar5iv HTML mirror. This is a description of the array itself, unlike the site record's current coordinate (a Nominatim geocode of the town of Delta, Utah, 60+ km away in places, precision_m 15000, explicitly documented there as 'NOT a survey point for the array') -- reported as a site coordinate correction candidate in the worklog. accuracy_m 6000 covers the one-decimal-degree rounding (+-0.05 degrees ~ 5.5 km at this latitude). The 507-station 1.2 km SD grid and the three fluorescence-detector sites (Black Rock Mesa, Long Ridge, Middle Drum) have widely repeated coordinates online, but every instance traces to a secondary/amateur-astronomy source (cleardarksky.com, itself Wikipedia's own citation for these values) rather than an official TA page or paper fetched this session, so they are not drawn (see worklog backlog).
name: Telescope Array (reference point)
notes: 507-counter 1.2 km grid and the three fluorescence-detector sites (Black Rock Mesa, Long Ridge, Middle Drum) are not drawn: their widely repeated coordinates trace only to a hobbyist astronomy site (cleardarksky.com), not to an official TA page or paper fetched this session (telescopearray.org and known mirrors were unreachable). summary.plain: The Telescope Array ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory near Delta, Utah, shown here as a single reference point at the array's own published centre.
